keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Picentes row; the page has no infobox area. South Picenum by the provinces of Macerata, Fermo, Ascoli Piceno and Teramo (about 7,300 km2 by the gazetteer); the Picentes 'had no predominant inhabited centre'. The page's Picenum reaches north to the Foglia, but the Senones occupied it 'north of the Esino' in 390 (the Pesaro-Ancona strip is the umbri/senones dossiers'). Soft edges.

correction.text: South Picenum: 'the Adriatic Sea south of Ancona was Picenum'; Macerata, Fermo, Ascoli Piceno and Teramo; allied to Rome from 299, in revolt from 269

keyframe_review.note: Same shape; from 299 the Picentes are allies of Rome by treaty (tint, vassal_start 299, vassal_end 269 when they revolted), the Picentine war of 269-268 is a contest inside it, and in 268 Rome annexes the shape except Ancona and Asculum, which kept allied status.

region.text: Picenum, 'all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo', except Ancona and Asculum

ledger.note: c. 500 BC: the Picentes 'in the area between the Foglia and Aterno rivers'; 'Picenum including all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo'; they 'had no predominant inhabited centre, and therefore had no need for a capital'. No formation date; 500 is a placeholder before the treaty of 299. The page's Picenum is wider, 'all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo' (Foglia to Aterno), but the Senones took 'Picenum north of the Esino' in 390 and that strip (Rimini to Ancona) is drawn once, as Umbrian, in the umbri dossier and as Senonian afterwards; this dossier draws South Picenum only.

ledger.note: 299 BC: 'When in 299 BC the Romans captured Nequinum, they also concluded a treaty with the Picentes'; the Picentes become allies of Rome, tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start picentes 299).

region.text: Picenum, 'all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo', except Ancona and Asculum

ledger.note: 269-268 BC: 'The Picene revolt against Rome began in 269 BC, the "Picentine war"'; the consuls Appius Claudius Russus and Publius Sempronius Sophus sent against them. The treaty of 299 ('they also concluded a treaty with the Picentes') had made them allies (tint, roman-republic vassal_start 299).

ledger.note: 269 BC: the Picentes 'broke the alliance and in 269 BC revolted and started the Picentine war' (roman-republic /ledger/29 ends the tie in 268, with the annexation).

ledger.note: 268 BC: 'Rome then annexed the rest of Picenum, except Ancona and Asculum, which kept allied status'; civitas sine suffragio 268, 'civitas optimo iure' 241; part of the population deported to the Silarus (Picentia) and Lake Fucino; Firmum 264.

notes: New state. Picenum is the roman-republic dossier's 268 gain region; the Senones' coast is removed c. 390 at confidence 1. Allied status 299-268 is tinted from roman-republic.
